correctness.rationale: The unique beta root follows from strictly increasing Bernoulli rate beyond the mean. Uniform Stirling and geometric lower-tail expansion give a log N saddle with prefactor (log N)^(-1/2), verifying the negative half-log-log shift. The one-round exact inclusion probability (d)_a(N-d)_(h-a)/(N)_h gives multiplicative O(log N/N) joint-history comparisons; factorial moments yield Poisson defects. Conditional binomial coupling yields nonpositive covariance of pair defects, proving an early-tail bound, and the binomial boundary recurrence supplies geometric late tails. Uniform integrability proves additive moment laws. The separate standard-library checker passed 3326 assertions, including exact finite transition checks and numerical saddlepoint diagnostics; finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The logarithmically diverging target multiplicity is naturally motivated by repeated pooled coverage and differs qualitatively from fixed multiplicity: a binary relative-entropy saddle controls late deficiencies. The half-log-log correction diverges relative to an O(1) terminal window, and the parameter-dependent lattice ratio and additive moment formulas quantify systematic centering error and final-round variability. The theorem covers every positive alpha and every interior limiting batch fraction, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
